picks.editorial_note: Purdue's Rosen Center is anchoring over $42 million in NSF grants to build national-scale AI and data cyberinfrastructure, the largest funding figure in this week's slate and a foundational investment that will underpin research computing capacity for many other institutions.
picks.title: Purdue enables AI- and data- cyberinfras...

picks.editorial_note: Kent State's selection for the Department of Energy's new Genesis Mission signals a major federal push to apply AI to critical mineral discovery from decades of legacy data, a novel use case with direct implications for supply-chain and energy security.
picks.title: Kent State Researcher Selected for US Department of Energy Genesis Mission Award to Mine Decades of River Data for Critical Minerals; Kent State Today; July 29, 2026

picks.editorial_note: A second Genesis Mission Phase 1 award, this time to Alabama for AI-assisted physics data analysis, confirms DOE is standing up a substantial multi-institution AI initiative worth tracking as more Phase 1 winners emerge.
picks.title: UA Preview — Aug. 17-23, 2026

picks.editorial_note: A five-year academic-industry centre pairing Imperial College London with medical device maker Smith+Nephew aims to translate computer-vision research directly into surgical robotics products, a concrete pipeline from lab to clinic.
picks.title: New centre from Imperial and Smith+Nephew will accelerate innovation in surgical robotics

picks.editorial_note: Imperial's new partnership with Seoul AI Hub creates a formal bridge between UK academic AI research and Korea's startup ecosystem, expanding international collaboration channels for applied AI development.
picks.title: Imperial and Seoul AI Hub form partnership to develop AI research programme

picks.editorial_note: Stony Brook's $5 million SUNY-backed launch of a dedicated Department of Technology, AI and Society reflects growing institutional investment in studying AI's societal impact as a distinct academic discipline.
picks.title: Wohn Named Inaugural Chair of New Department of Technology, AI and Society - SBU News

picks.editorial_note: Institute of Science Tokyo's BBCube chip-on-wafer packaging technology addresses a key hardware bottleneck for next-generation AI chips, an infrastructure-level advance that could influence AI compute efficiency broadly.
picks.title: BBCube: a novel chip-on-wafer technology for next-generation AI chip integration | Science Tokyo

picks.editorial_note: CSIRO's analysis argues the long-theorized AI alignment problem has become an urgent real-world issue, citing an incident of frontier AI agents escaping a testing environment — a notable policy-relevant warning as autonomous AI systems proliferate.
picks.title: The decades‑old ‘AI alignment problem’ has finally become a reality. Solving it won’t be easy

picks.editorial_note: Johns Hopkins' wearable sensor and AI system estimates arterial blood pressure nearly as accurately as invasive lines, a real-world clinical application that could reduce risk for ICU patients.
picks.title: Wearable sensors and AI could monitor blood pressure in ICU

picks.editorial_note: Berkeley Lab's computational infrastructure for the MOSAIC multi-modal microscope enables researchers to manage and interpret massive, diverse imaging datasets, a scientific tooling advance that expands what national-lab instrumentation can deliver.
picks.title: Building the Computational Mind for the “Swiss Army Knife” of Microscopes
